sentence: A thin one, built after the harm.
claim: A tan gives only modest protection: about the equivalent of SPF 3–4.
source_title: Are there benefits to a base tan? (Harvard Health Publishing, Harvard Medical School)
note: Excerpt (Harvard Health): going out with a base tan 'is equivalent to wearing a sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of 3 to 4'. Mayo's FAQ: 'modest protection … does not come close to' sunscreen. 'A thin one' carries it.

sentence: A thin one, built after the harm.
claim: A tan develops in response to UV damage to skin cells: it follows the injury, it does not precede it.
source_title: HHS response to a request for correction of CDC's tanning wording (ASPE, HHS); CDC: a tan is the body's response to UV injury
note: Excerpt (CDC wording as quoted by HHS's response to a correction request): a tan is the body's response to injury, skin cells signalling they have been hurt by UV by producing more pigment; HHS kept the wording as 'scientifically accurate, as exposure to UV radiation has been shown in molecular studies to damage DNA in skin cells'. Cross-check: Mayo, 'any change in skin color from tanning is a sign of damage from UV radiation'.

sentence: Sunlight carries ultraviolet, and its shorter rays reach the living cells under the dead layer.
claim: The shorter-wavelength ultraviolet (UVB) is absorbed mostly in the epidermis; its DNA damage is found mainly in the living keratinocytes above the basal layer (UVA reaches deeper).
source_title: Agar NS, Halliday GM, Barnetson RS, et al. The basal layer in human squamous tumors harbors more UVA than UVB fingerprint mutations. PNAS 2004;101:4954–4959
note: Excerpt: UVB-fingerprint mutations sat mostly in suprabasal cells, UVA-type mainly in the basal layer; UVA penetrates deeper than UVB. Screen shows 'UVB'. 'Under the dead layer' = the living epidermis just beneath the stratum corneum.

sentence: In under a trillionth of a second, one can fuse two letters of their DNA.
claim: UV light makes cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (two adjacent DNA bases, thymines, bonded together) within about 1 picosecond (a trillionth of a second) of absorption.
source_title: Schreier WJ, Schrader TE, Koller FO, Gilch P, Crespo-Hernández CE, Swaminathan VN, Carell T, Zinth W, Kohler B. Thymine dimerization in DNA is an ultrafast photoreaction. Science 2007;315:625–629
note: Excerpt: CPDs in all-thymine DNA (dT)18 'form within 1 ps' of excitation (femtosecond infrared spectroscopy). Measured in a model oligonucleotide, not in a cell: the screen says '< 1 ps · in DNA strands (lab)'. 'Can fuse' because only a small share of absorbed photons makes a dimer. 'Two letters' = two bases.

claim: Skin cells detect UV-induced DNA damage: the damage activates the p53 protein.
source_title: Cui R, Widlund HR, Feige E, et al. Central role of p53 in the suntan response and pathologic hyperpigmentation. Cell 2007;128:853–864 (press summary: ScienceDaily, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, 8 Mar 2007)
note: Excerpt: 'When p53 is activated in response to DNA damage from the sun's ultraviolet rays …'. 'The cell notices' is that activation.

sentence: A guardian protein switches on, and the cell sends a chemical message down to the pigment cells: make melanin.
claim: In keratinocytes, UV-activated p53 switches on the POMC gene, whose product is cut into α-MSH; α-MSH acts on melanocytes (the pigment cells, in the basal layer) and they make melanin.
source_title: Cui R, Widlund HR, Feige E, et al. Central role of p53 in the suntan response and pathologic hyperpigmentation. Cell 2007;128:853–864 (press summary: ScienceDaily, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, 8 Mar 2007)
note: Excerpt: p53 binds and increases transcription from POMC; POMC is cleaved into α-MSH, 'a hormone that then prompts production of melanin'; α-MSH rose about 30× after UV in mouse and human keratinocytes. 'A guardian protein' is p53's common name in biology ('guardian of the genome'); p53 and α-MSH are named on screen. 'Down to the pigment cells': melanocytes sit in the basal layer.

sentence: In Boston, mice whose skin cells lacked that guardian never tanned at all.
claim: In Cui et al. 2007, mice whose keratinocytes lacked p53 did not induce POMC after UV and did not tan.
source_title: Cui R, Widlund HR, Feige E, et al. Central role of p53 in the suntan response and pathologic hyperpigmentation. Cell 2007;128:853–864 (press summary: ScienceDaily, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, 8 Mar 2007)
note: Excerpt: 'when UV radiation was delivered to mice whose keratinocytes lacked p53, POMC production was not induced and the mice did not tan.' The work was at Dana-Farber / Harvard Medical School in Boston (David Fisher's lab). Mice, so the screen says 'in mice · Cui et al., 2007'.

sentence: So a tan isn't skin getting ready for the sun.
claim: Tanning is triggered by damage, not by an advance signal: there is no tan without prior UV injury to skin cells.
source_title: HHS response to a request for correction of CDC's tanning wording (ASPE, HHS); CDC: a tan is the body's response to UV injury
note: Follows from c2 and c7: the tan is downstream of DNA damage. 'Getting ready for the sun' is the base-tan idea (Harvard Health: 'little evidence' a base tan protects; Mayo FAQ the same).

sentence: It's skin answering damage already done.
claim: A tan is the skin's response to DNA damage that has already happened.
source_title: HHS response to a request for correction of CDC's tanning wording (ASPE, HHS); CDC: a tan is the body's response to UV injury
note: As c2 (CDC, Mayo): 'even a tan indicates damage to your skin'; Cui 2007: p53 activated by DNA damage drives it.

sentence: Over the next few days, the melanin settles over each nucleus like a tiny parasol.
claim: Delayed tanning (new melanin, driven mostly by UVB) becomes visible about 48–72 hours after exposure.
source_title: Peer-reviewed article on UV-induced pigmentation (PMC2593890; a person confirms its title when opening the link)
note: Excerpt (peer-reviewed review): 'UVB radiation causes the delayed tanning reaction that takes several days or longer to develop'; other summaries put visible onset at about 48–72 h. 'Over the next few days' carries it; the screen shows '48–72 h'. Immediate pigment darkening (UVA, existing melanin) is a separate effect, not shown.

sentence: Over the next few days, the melanin settles over each nucleus like a tiny parasol.
claim: Keratinocytes take up melanin from melanocytes and arrange it above the nucleus as a supranuclear cap, which shields the DNA from UV by absorbing and scattering it.
source_title: The journey of the pigment melanin from one cell to another (NOVA Medical School, Lisbon; Barral lab, 2023)
note: Excerpt: pigment 'is transferred to neighboring cells called keratinocytes … These keratinocytes arrange the melanin on the top of their nuclei'. Cross-check (Opsin 3 paper, PMC9984416, search excerpt): the supranuclear cap shields DNA by absorbing and scattering UV. 'Like a tiny parasol' is the image; the drawing is badged 'illustration'.

sentence: Together, a whole tan adds up to about SPF three or four.
claim: A tan's protection is about the equivalent of SPF 3–4.
source_title: Are there benefits to a base tan? (Harvard Health Publishing, Harvard Medical School)
note: Excerpt as c1. Other sources: 'SPF 4 at most' (Mayo, via a dermatology practice), 'less than 4' (an EPA adviser, Axios). The screen shows 'SPF ≈ 3–4 · estimate'. No comparison to any product is made or implied.

sentence: Each parasol is about as wide as its nucleus: a dozen side by side would span a sheet of paper.
claim: A keratinocyte nucleus is about 8.6 µm across (estimate from reflectance confocal microscopy; whole cells 15–35 µm); the melanin cap covers the nucleus, so it is about that wide.
source_title: Gareau DS. Automated identification of epidermal keratinocytes in reflectance confocal microscopy. J Biomed Opt 2011;16(3):030502
note: Excerpt: 'the mean nuclear diameter (a = 8.6 μm) … compares well to the published diameter for the entire cell: 15 to 35 μm'; a model-fitted estimate (± 2.8 µm). The cap's width as the nucleus's is the cap's definition (it sits over the nucleus); shown 'about 9 µm'. Computed: 100 ÷ 8.6 ≈ 11.6 → 'a dozen side by side' (about).

sentence: Each parasol is about as wide as its nucleus: a dozen side by side would span a sheet of paper.
claim: Standard 80 gsm copy paper is about 100 µm thick; 17 µm is about 0.17 of it ('thinner than a fifth', computed).
source_title: Papers and boards: category and standards (WJEC, UK education resource)
note: As Outer Layer No. 001's paper claim. Excerpt: copying paper 80 gsm, 100 microns. Everyday reference; not a skin claim.

claim: A tan gives only modest protection (about SPF 3–4).
source_title: Are there benefits to a base tan? (Harvard Health Publishing, Harvard Medical School)

sentence: It's how your skin remembers the light.
claim: A tan is the skin's lasting pigment response to the UV damage it has received.
source_title: HHS response to a request for correction of CDC's tanning wording (ASPE, HHS); CDC: a tan is the body's response to UV injury
note: As c2 and c9; 'remembers' is the image for a response that follows and outlasts the exposure (days to weeks).
